problem_text:
A logistics firm is organizing a fleet of delivery drones for a three-day aerial supply mission. They must select a combination of cargo packages to maximize total utility points while adhering to the total payload weight constraint.

The available packages are:
* Package A: weight 48kg, utility 116 points
* Package B: weight 25kg, utility 110 points
* Package C: weight 21kg, utility 104 points
* Package D: weight 12kg, utility 264 points
* Package E: weight 43kg, utility 87 points
* Package F: weight 40kg, utility 268 points
* Package G: weight 27kg, utility 126 points
* Package H: weight 1kg, utility 37 points
* Package I: weight 28kg, utility 26 points
* Package J: weight 42kg, utility 79 points
* Package K: weight 33kg, utility 53 points
* Package L: weight 27kg, utility 168 points
* Package M: weight 22kg, utility 106 points
* Package N: weight 46kg, utility 41 points
* Package O: weight 22kg, utility 80 points
* Package P: weight 21kg, utility 150 points
* Package Q: weight 32kg, utility 256 points

Furthermore, due to compatibility requirements, exactly one of Package A and Package B must be included in the shipment.

If Package C is selected, it necessitates special handling equipment that reduces the effective payload capacity of the drone fleet by 10 kg.
The maximum allowable total payload weight is 343 kg. The firm must determine the optimal set of packages to dispatch.
